policies.title: Schedule 4 named ordinary passports: visa-free entry
policies.summary: Saint Lucia’s current Revised Laws Schedule 4 directly exempts the named country nationals, including the non-Haitian CARICOM cohort. Singapore is exempt only for stays under 15 days.
conditions: Applies to the expressly named passport issuers and the named non-Haitian CARICOM foreign-member cohort only.
Singapore is visa-free only for stays of less than 15 days.
Haiti is expressly excluded by Schedule 4’s temporary visa-requirement carve-out.
The statutory waiver does not establish citizenship, residence, work, study, transit, crew, diplomatic, official/service, special-document or individual admissibility treatment.

policies.title: Covered EU ordinary passports: reciprocal short-stay visa-free access
policies.summary: The official Government notice states that the EU–Saint Lucia agreement gives EU citizens the identical reciprocal short-stay visa-free rights. The named 26 covered EU States supplement Schedule 4.
conditions: Valid ordinary passports only; stay may not exceed 90 days in any 180-day period.
Paid activity is excluded and ordinary border, health, security and admissibility controls continue to apply.
Ireland and the United Kingdom are outside this agreement; their treatment is separately stated in Schedule 4.

policies.title: Brazilian ordinary passports: reciprocal short-stay visa-free access
policies.summary: Brazil’s Foreign Ministry treaty record identifies the reciprocal ordinary-passport short-stay waiver with Saint Lucia as in force from 14 January 2024. It is easier than the older Schedule 2 arrival-visa entry.
conditions: The bilateral instrument is limited to holders of ordinary passports and is recorded by Brazil’s Foreign Ministry as in force from 14 January 2024.
The reviewed treaty record does not state a duration, purpose, paid-activity, admission, document or route rule; the agreement and Saint Lucian immigration controls still govern those details.

Schedule 2 still lists Brazil for a visa that may be issued on arrival. The later in-force reciprocal waiver is used as the easier route; the unreconciled domestic schedule is a material recheck risk.
This is not a citizenship, residence, work, study, transit, crew, diplomatic, official/service, special-document or individual-admissibility rule.

policies.title: Schedule 2 named ordinary passports: visa may be issued on arrival
policies.summary: The current Revised Laws expressly place these named nationalities in Schedule 2, under which the visa may be obtained on arrival.
conditions: The statute says the visa may be issued on arrival; entry is not guaranteed and immigration, document, health, security and admissibility requirements remain applicable.
Brazil is excluded because the in-force bilateral ordinary-passport waiver is the easier route. Georgia is excluded because its published waiver material lacks an entry-into-force date.
This policy does not establish eVisa, ETA, work, residence, study, transit, crew, diplomatic, official/service or special-document treatment.

policies.title: Schedule 3 named ordinary passports: visa required before arrival
policies.summary: The current Revised Laws expressly require these named nationalities to obtain a visa before arrival.
conditions: An advance visa is required under Schedule 3; it is not an eVisa or an unconditional visa-on-arrival route.
The current external-affairs service describes an application workflow and a case-specific airport possibility, not a nationality-wide electronic or arrival alternative to this Schedule 3 rule.
This policy excludes citizenship, residence, work, study, transit, crew, diplomatic, official/service, special-document and individual admissibility treatment.
